races.name: John Smith's Nursery

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter here; won over 6f at York on good in its last run which is the key qualifier, though the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence — it may not reproduce that form if asked to dictate again having raced from a slightly different position; 14 days since last run is a positive freshness angle for Eve Johnson Houghton.

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's two-year-old has won over 6f on standard ground and returns after 42 days off — a rest that can sharpen juvenile sprinters; races prominently and is unexposed enough to have improved, with Oisin Orr a considerable asset.

runners_data.name: Dubai Champion
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's lightly-raced two-year-old won over 5f on soft last time, step up to 6f on faster ground is a query — but placed twice in three starts on good and Andrew Mullen is a competent judge of pace at this track; racing prominently suits the likely shape.

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent performer has nine runs showing eight outings on similar going and a form string dotted with wins and places at exactly this trip; races prominently, suits the dominant shape of this race, and Easterby's 15/104 14-day strike rate indicates a yard in decent form.

runners_data.name: Ballisty
runners_data.note: Jack Jones' runner naturally wants to race up with the pace but with so many prominent types in this field it is likely to find itself operating a position further back than ideal; posted placed efforts in its last three starts and the 0W2P record reflects consistency without a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Boleto
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends this winner of a 6f good-ground race here, and the form credentials are clear — but as a natural front-runner squeezed out of its preferred position by the surplus of pace in this field, it will have to do something tactically different; Rossa Ryan is the right jockey to manage that compromise.

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.note: The unknown quantity in the field with a 'U' style classification and form that shows a step back in grade from 7f; Billy Garritty takes a low-profile booking and the recent best finish of third suggests it is capable of threatening but hasn't yet found the consistency needed to win at this level.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up horse is the truest back-marker in the race, racing from off the pace on good ground three times recently with a best finish of third; on a straight six this pattern demands a strong early gallop to manufacture the gap it needs, which this race shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Brandenburg
runners_data.note: Stephen Hanlon's runner was dismissed at 12/1 last time before winning on soft at 5f, making the step up to 6f on faster ground a significant question; despite being a natural prominent racer, it is redistributed to midfield in this analysis given the field's front-end congestion, and 68 days off adds uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: York's straight six on Good to Firm ground is a true test of speed and stamina, and this nine-runner nursery is loaded with prominent-racing types. Super Tuscan is the confirmed front runner and, without any genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a lung-busting pace — the kind that often plays into the hands of horses tracking close behind. Furturra is the standout with eight runs from nine in similar going conditions and a profile built around racing prominently on good ground over this exact trip, making her the natural beneficiary of an honest but not frenetic pace. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all get their natural positions: Brandenburg, Boleto and Ballisty are all genuine prominent horses but are likely to be shuffled back or race in a manufactured midfield, meaning their redistribution suppresses the likelihood of a genuine late-closer scenario materialising. The race shape strongly favours horses tracking Super Tuscan in second or third — a prominent, ground-efficient, patient-but-close profile is the one to back here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Super Tuscan sets a fair but unforced pace and the winner times a run from close pursuit in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Super Tuscan's controlled lead creates a false-pace illusion that rewards a horse sitting a length or two off, able to pounce before the distance marker; the straight six at York demands a prominent position to sustain any challenge on fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Super Tuscan gets completely unchallenged and converts a well-judged lead into a wire-to-wire success.
scenarios.body: With no horse in the field willing or able to push Super Tuscan for the lead, a comfortable gallop allows it to conserve energy and sprint clear inside the final furlong; this shape is plausible but partially discounted as Super Tuscan carries a STYLE_FIT tag suggesting it may not fully reproduce its best from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens enough to string the field out and leave a gap for a late-finishing effort from behind the main group.
scenarios.body: This requires horses like Rbflying or Social Spirit to find more than their bare form suggests, and demands a stronger pace than Super Tuscan alone is likely to set; it remains a low-probability shape as the genuine late runners in this race have limited class to confirm it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types jostles for position early and creates an uneven, stop-start early pace that scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: Boleto, Ballisty and Brandenburg all want to race prominently and if they push forward aggressively the race could develop into a rough, bunched affair where positional luck dominates; in this messy scenario, a horse with tactical versatility and experience over the course such as Furturra or a lightly-raced improver like Brandenburg could benefit.

watchPoints.text: Furturra and Rbflying are trained by Tim Easterby who has two runners in this race — watch for any signs of a market move on the less-fancied Rbflying as Easterby fields a dual runner scenario that could obscure which horse the yard prefers.

Brandenburg has been off 68 days since winning on soft over 5f — a sharp class and going rise in its second ever start; watch how it loads and settles early, as inexperienced horses returning fresh after a break can be unpredictable in large-field sprint conditions.

Boleto and Ballisty are both natural prominent types likely to find themselves shuffled wider or further back at the start than they prefer — watch the initial stalls opening for scrimmaging, which could compromise early positions and amplify their STYLE_FIT disadvantage.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race — a fast surface will favour horses with a high TS (top speed) rating and smooth, economic action; Social Spirit's only comparable going effort produced a fifth on soft, meaning this surface is notably quicker than anything it has faced.

Big Cigar returns after 42 days off for a yard with a 7/56 14-day strike rate — not a powerhouse in-form stable, but Fahey's two-year-old sprinters are capable of running well fresh; watch the market closely in the final 20 minutes before the off.

races.name: John Smith's Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: David Of Athens
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter with solid course-and-distance form (won York 1m on Good), Pierre-Louis Jamin takes over after 105 days off — returns fresher than rivals but the layoff is a flag on a 142lb weight; his ability to dictate entirely suits this shape and the style-fit tag reflects the peculiarity of his mapped role rather than any style conflict for a horse that is genuinely front-running.

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope reunites with a horse who handles Good ground well (13 of 15 sim-going appearances on similar), sits naturally prominent, and has strong place consistency at 1m — his 24-day freshener suits and O'Meara's 7 winners in 14 days signals a yard in form.

runners_data.name: Checkandchallenge
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist who has head gear (p) listed and whose recent form reads 39-060 over this course and trip — limited recent ability to deliver from the back on Good ground with only 3 places from 15 similar-going starts; 24 days since last run is routine.

runners_data.name: Cosi Bello
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has a quiet 14-day record (0/17) but this 4-year-old showed real versatility winning at 7f and placing at 8f on Good ground; Paddy Bradley takes the ride and the horse's prominent style fits the race shape, though the step back to 1m after recent 7f campaign needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Apiarist
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 5-year-old has a poor recent record at 1m on Good (0 wins, 0 places from 4 similar-going runs); the prominent style is a fit but form figures of 413060 show inconsistency and Tom Eaves will need to find a pocket just off the pace to extract anything meaningful.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby picks up the ride on a hold-up horse who has been campaigned extensively over 10f and 12f — dropping back to 1m on Good To Firm is a potential stamina reversal in his favour, but the going record (4 from 7 on similar) is moderate and the recent 706-00 form string is discouraging.

runners_data.name: The Lost King
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 4-year-old is in excellent recent form (121340) and has course form at 8f on Standard/similar going (1W2P); PJ McDonald navigates a field with a high-pressure midfield and the horse's prominent style fits what the race shape demands from second or third position.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 4-year-old drops from 9f back to 8f on similar ground (6 from 9 appearances), having shown only a single win and place at this sort of trip — Oisin Orr handles him out of the hold-up position and 35 days between runs is routine, but the declining form string (93-500) is a concern.

runners_data.name: First Principle
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 4-year-old wears a tongue-tie (tp) and has clear placed form at 8f on Standard (1W2P) — a natural prominent racer who, with so many similar types in this field, will realistically be shuffled to a midfield slot and asked to race out of role; 47 days off may have refreshed him but the style displacement dilutes his chance.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: Has won twice at this 8f trip and shown consistent placed form, but competes here at an OR of 90 with 16 days since last run — a natural front-runner who will be pushed back into the midfield pack by the surplus of prominent rivals, forcing Ray Dawson to adapt tactically and reducing the horse's effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Bragbor
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's 5-year-old has produced placed efforts in similar company but almost exclusively at 10f+ (4 of last 5 runs); the sim-going record on Good is a single effort from 10 similar-ground starts and the Warren Fentiman claim (3lb) is unlikely to offset the tactical squeeze this horse will face racing back at 8f.

runners_data.name: New Image
runners_data.note: O'Meara's 6-year-old has 2 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-going runs, suggesting class but inconsistency — Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) partners a horse whose front-running instinct will be suppressed by the depth of pace, and the declining form string (6-3057) offers limited confidence in a race of this competitiveness.

runners_data.name: Gentle George
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old dropping from 6f to 8f for the first time in a handicap, having only ever won over 5-6f — Cam Hardie handles a horse that is a natural pace type now mapped to midfield because of pace congestion, and the distance extension to 1m on Good To Firm with a declining recent record (116-00) raises serious suitability questions.

races.paceDynamic: David Of Athens is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good To Firm ground at York. The field holds significantly more prominent-minded types than can realistically secure their preferred position — First Principle, Gentle George, Mr Swivell, Bragbor and New Image are all natural front-to-prominent racers who will be squeezed back into midfield roles against their instincts, creating a bunched, compressed midfield pack rather than a strung-out field. David Of Athens is therefore likely to stride along at a measured tempo with a loose lead, dictating terms without being seriously tested for the opening six furlongs, which will set up a one-pace gallop to the line rather than a brutal stamina test. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken from just off the pace — those able to press David Of Athens in second or third and respond when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs will be best positioned, while genuine hold-up horses and the redistributed prominent types stuck in midfield face an unfavourable tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Steady Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If David Of Athens bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest but not extreme, setting up a test of finishing quality over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: David Of Athens controls every yard at a metronomic gallop and the race becomes a tactical one-pace affair decided by acceleration in the final quarter-mile; horses pressing him in second and third have first run and can exploit any hesitation.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Late
scenarios.trigger: If the true prominent runners — Cerulean Bay and The Lost King — successfully track David Of Athens and unleash a decisive move rounding the final bend.
scenarios.body: Cerulean Bay and The Lost King, both proven at this course and trip, latch onto the leader's quarters and hit the front with enough momentum to deny David Of Athens; their class and recent form at the 1m trip makes this a credible counter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Exploits Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough early to string the field out and a hold-up or mid-division runner threads through late on the Good To Firm surface.
scenarios.body: Checkandchallenge or Khafiz, sitting quietly in rear, could benefit if the compressed midfield opens up inside the final furlong on quick ground — however their recent form figures are uninspiring and reliance on traffic clearing adds significant risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If several of the natural prominent runners — Gentle George, Mr Swivell, Bragbor — fight for position early and inject an unexpected injection of pace that disrupts David Of Athens's rhythm.
scenarios.body: A contested lead would compress the margins and potentially set up a stronger late challenge from hold-up types, but these horses are all mapped out of their natural role with modest recent form figures and the scenario depends on runners performing against type.

watchPoints.text: David Of Athens is 105 days absent and takes on a full 13-runner field at York — if he sets a muddling pace and ties up late, the prominent horses tracking him (Cerulean Bay, The Lost King) will swoop past in the final furlong.

The cluster of natural prominent runners — First Principle, Mr Swivell, Bragbor, Gentle George and New Image — will jostle for positions they cannot all occupy; watch for crowding and checking in the early stages as the field settles heading towards the first bend.

Gentle George has never been asked to stay a mile and races off a declining sequence (116-00) — any sign of greenness or stopping in the final furlong could cause interference to runners in the congested midfield pack.

Good To Firm ground is confirmed for the 2:39 race — horses with strong sim-going records (Cerulean Bay 13/15, The Lost King placed at similar) hold a surface advantage over rivals like Apiarist (4/15) and Bragbor (1/10) on comparable going.

Trainer angle: David O'Meara has 7 winners from 47 runners in the past 14 days — with both Cerulean Bay and New Image in this field, the stable is live across the board and worth tracking for market moves before the off.

races.name: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Washington Heights
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Kevin Ryan who has strong course-and-distance form but recent finishes read 0-0-8 suggesting flat patches; sim-going record is solid at 13/15 but the 42-day absence is a mild flag, and on a relatively controlled pace at York's five he may find the winner gone before he can close.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old is the race's only confirmed front-runner and shapes to lead from the gates under Mulrennan, but her STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine caution — if the pace is contested hard she could be worn down; her recent win at this course and distance on good is the key positive angle.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been running consistently at this level for Quinn, though his recent form string of 6-0-4-9-0 is patchy and his two wins in similar going came in less competitive company; his trainer's 14-day strike-rate of 1/22 is modest.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's four-year-old is a natural front-runner with three wins from ten on similar going, carrying a visor for the first time today; displaced to midfield on the pace map due to the crowded prominent division, he will want to push forward and his STYLE_FIT tag means his chance depends on whether he can reclaim that forward berth.

runners_data.name: Redorange
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's four-year-old has an eye-catching going record of 14/15 runs on good to firm, underpinning his suitability for today; genuine prominent runner whose single win at this course level keeps him interesting, though his recent form of 8-7-8-1-4 is inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old is equipped with a visor and has consistent good-ground form but her 0/3 placed record from prominent positions tells its own story — she shows but does not win; a 23-length last at Goodwood last time out is hard to overlook even accounting for that being over 5f on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Bethell's six-year-old has two wins on similar going and is a natural prominent racer who has been pushed into the midfield section of the map because the prominent slots are full; Daniel Tudhope is a course specialist and this horse's 1/5/1 in her last five runs at this trip gives her real live claims if she can fight to the front.

runners_data.name: Dickensian
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old posted a career-best when winning on good ground over York's five last time and all eight career runs have come on good — a perfectly matched profile for today; despite being pushed back on the map from his natural prominent position, his recent form figures of 3-3-3-1 make him one of the most in-form horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old has placed at this level twice over five furlongs on good ground, but two consecutive beaten efforts including a 16th at York last time are hard to ignore; the Joanna Mason booking is notable but this horse's sim-going hit-rate of 6/10 and winless record at Listed level suggest he is one for each-way framing at best.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old runs without headgear and has a recent second at this trip on good ground to her name, giving her a legitimate placed chance; however, her sim-going record of only 3/15 is low and the trainer's 0/4 run in the past fortnight is a quiet flag.

runners_data.name: Luna A Inbhir Nis
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's four-year-old arrives fresh off a run just seven days ago, and while her 5 wins from 9 on good going is the strongest pace-fit metric in the field, she is a natural up-with-the-pace type squeezed into the midfield draw by the volume of prominent runners; if she gets her position she can be competitive, if she doesn't she is compromised.

runners_data.name: Military Code
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's three-year-old is a hold-up type with a 7/7 sim-going record and two runner-up finishes in his last five, but he operates on the back foot and needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in the leaders in the final furlong; the Connor Planas booking is a step down from Appleby's usual jockey choices.

runners_data.name: Miss Attitude
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's six-year-old wears a tongue-tie and a pads combination and has been competing consistently at this level without winning — her one win in 15 on similar going underlines the trend; a hold-up type who needs the race to fall apart in front of her, which is unlikely in a relatively controlled-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's lightly-raced three-year-old has three wins from four starts on good ground and a form string reading 1-1-3-1-6 is genuinely strong; she is by nature a pace-pressing type pushed rearward by the volume of prominent horses, and whether she can find her natural position early is the key question around her chance.

runners_data.name: Revival Power
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has three wins from eight on good and his recent record of 1-1-5-7-0 shows a rapid loss of form after a promising early campaign; another natural front-runner repositioned in the map due to pace congestion, and the STYLE_FIT flag means his chance is heavily contingent on securing that forward berth from the draw.

races.paceDynamic: American Affair is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Paul Mulrennan likely to press for the early lead, she shapes to control the tempo on good-to-firm ground over York's straight five furlongs — a surface and track that rewards those who can dominate from the gates. However, this field is stacked with prominent types: Dickensian, Luna A Inbhir Nis, Revival Power, Naana's Shadow, Lexington Blitz, and Azure Angel are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who have been mapped to midfield positions simply because there is not enough room for all of them to race where they want, meaning the early stages are likely to be sharper than the lone-leader tag implies. The sustainable, unexposed pace set by American Affair — rather than a true breakneck gallop — will compress the field and reduce the premium on raw closing ability, keeping hold-up horses like Washington Heights and Military Code honest. This race shape most favours horses who can secure a prominent berth or track the pace in the first two or three positions, as the relatively controlled tempo over a flat five furlongs at York will reward those able to quicken from a handy spot rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: American Affair Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If American Affair secures the lead unchallenged and the prominent types settle into a rhythm behind rather than fighting for position.
scenarios.body: American Affair dictates a sustainable gallop, stretching the field out gradually and ensuring the finish is a test of maintained speed rather than a late sprint; horses who track her closely and quicken in the final furlong — particularly those with strong good-to-firm form — will finish fastest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Into Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of prominent types jockey for position early, burning pace and leaving the race a flat-out sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The early scramble for prominent positions — with Naana's Shadow, Revival Power, and Luna A Inbhir Nis all wanting to race up with the pace — will quicken the tempo beyond American Affair's ideal, resulting in a ragged sprint finish that opens the door for hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to take the sting out of the leaders but not so fast as to set up a pure sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting third or fourth — close enough to benefit from the pace but with energy in reserve — is able to sweep through the final furlong as the front two tie up; the good-to-firm ground and flat York five furlongs makes this a realistic outcome for a horse with strong recent form at the trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a gap for closers to pick off tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Washington Heights or Military Code, forced wide and held up, find a late surge as the prominent types exhaust themselves; this is a low-probability shape given most closers here are not natural hold-up types and the track does not favour long-range finishing runs.

watchPoints.text: American Affair holds the key pace position but if Naana's Shadow, Revival Power, or Luna A Inbhir Nis — all natural front-runners repositioned in the map — push to the front early, the pace will be far sharper than the lone-leader scenario implies, fundamentally changing the race shape.

Dickensian's profile is strikingly well-matched to today — good ground, York five furlongs, form figures of 3-3-3-1 — but he is mapped to midfield despite being a natural prominent racer; watch how quickly Shane Gray sends him forward from the stalls, as his chance depends entirely on reclaiming that position.

Azure Angel's trainer Edward Bethell has a 14-day strike-rate of 3/32 and Daniel Tudhope is a powerful booking at York; if she jumps cleanly and gets to her natural prominent position, her two wins on similar going over this course and trip make her a live market mover worth monitoring pre-race.

Luna A Inbhir Nis runs for the second time in seven days under Katie Scott, whose 14-day record stands at only 1/15 — watch for any market drift that suggests connections are not expecting a peak performance on this quick turnaround.

Lexington Blitz runs in headgear today for Robert Cowell and is a three-time winner on similar going; his STYLE_FIT flag means his chance is conditional on pushing forward past his mapped position, so his drawn stall number and early jump will be a key tell in the opening strides.

races.name: John Smith's Cup (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Respond
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two recent wins at this trip on similar ground; Andrew Balding and PJ McDonald is a potent combination and the hood (hg:h) may sharpen focus — sits ideally for a race run at Warrant Holder's tempo.

runners_data.name: Warrant Holder
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Gosden yard in solid current form (6/48 T14) and recent 12f win on good gives confidence, but racing slightly outside natural style here and faces a stiff task if the 22-runner field crowds early.

runners_data.name: Yabher
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner back after 70 days but returns with a sharp form line of four wins from seven on good ground including two over this course-and-distance equivalent; natural tracker who should slot in smoothly.

runners_data.name: Thunder Run
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent form (40-720) and struggles at this level on good ground historically — poor sim-going record (3W from 10P on fast) makes this hard to back with confidence.

runners_data.name: Danger Bay
runners_data.note: In career-best form with three wins from his last five starts including a 10f Good ground win last time; Edward Bethell yard punching well (3/32 T14) and Tudhope is an excellent big-field handler.

runners_data.name: Will Scarlet
runners_data.note: Won two of his last five at 10-12f including on good ground; the hood (hg:p) has been a feature of recent wins and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim makes the weight attractive — genuine each-way contender tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Hand Of God
runners_data.note: Decent stamina profile with a recent 10f Good win (OR=101); Lewis Edmunds takes over after a 57-day break which bears watching, but the form profile suggests he handles fast ground well and has the class to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Quai De Bethune
runners_data.note: Won on Good last time out at 10f but has finished sixth both times over softer; the hg:h flag and a return to fast ground could help, though trainer T14 of 0/12 is a mild flag — likely to race forward despite midfield mapping.

runners_data.name: Dain Ma Nut In
runners_data.note: Returning after a long 142-day absence which is a clear concern; when fresh he has won twice on Good ground, and over 10f the stamina is proven — needs to handle the layoff but the trainer trend is poor (0/5 T14).

runners_data.name: Auld Toon Loon
runners_data.note: Has won on Good at 10f but recent form (01-837) has tailed off; his natural want is to be prominent but with so many others seeking that ground, he is more likely to be shuffled back than he'd prefer — form figures also show limited recent impact on fast surfaces.

runners_data.name: Raammee
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and comes up markedly in trip from an 8f base — the step to 10f here is unproven; a true front-runner by inclination, he will struggle to find his natural berth in a 22-runner field, and his sim-going record (0W, 1P) at this level on fast ground adds doubt.

runners_data.name: Iron Fist
runners_data.note: Irish raider (Mrs John Harrington) who has run well on Good ground but finished third or worse in five of six attempts at 10f; by nature wants to be up with the pace but will be displaced, and the 49-day gap adds a second question mark.

runners_data.name: Have Secret
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good at 10f gives some ground comfort but recent form reads 4-5150, form has fallen away; inclined to race prominently but the headgear (hg:v) flag and current downward trajectory temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Believer
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old who won on Soft at 10f but has zero placings on Good-or-faster in 15 attempts on sim going — that sim-going blank is a hard data point to ignore regardless of natural style.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: Won a 12f Good ground race just seven days ago (LR:7d) which raises a freshness question, but course form over the distance is solid and a low weight (124lbs) compensates; James Owen yard is active (7/35 T14) and Rossa Ryan retains the ride.

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Modest form figures (1W/5P on sim going) and races over a shorter trip normally — stepping up from 7-8f base to 10f is an unproven stretch, and despite being a natural tracker he faces a tough ask in a higher-class handicap.

runners_data.name: Castle Stuart
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse (style=H) who finished second at 10f on Good last time; Barry McHugh and Fahey yard link up and if the pace is strong enough he has the profile to close late in the straight — one of the few true closers in the field.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good (OR=83) and has a string of placed efforts on the going, but the big step up from OR=83 into this company is significant; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a useful offset and the Goldie yard is in fair form.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and hit the frame at 10f at this course previously; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps, but the Fahey yard's current T14 ratio is stretched across three runners today — recent form (01565) doesn't inspire.

runners_data.name: Salam Dubawi
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose win came over 9f on Good; a second Goldie runner today (alongside Altareq) and the short 6-day turnaround after a recent outing should be noted — if the race sets up for late closers he has the profile to pick up the pieces.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up type (style=H) for Tim Easterby whose large stable is in strong current form (15/112 T14); form string 970348 is modest but the 3/11f Good placing suggests stamina is there, and Duran Fentiman keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly raced relative to the field; won over 10f on Good and placed at 12f recently (hg suggests improving), but Richard Hannon yard at 3/57 T14 is below par and racing against older, more seasoned handicappers is a stern test.

races.paceDynamic: Warrant Holder is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — on Good to Firm ground at York over 1m2½f, that means a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset rather than a contested burn. The large field is packed with natural prominent types — Auld Toon Loon, Raammee, Iron Fist, Have Secret, Fantasy Believer, Pearl River and others — but there is simply not enough room for all of them to slot in behind Warrant Holder, meaning several will be forced to either challenge forward and potentially stack pace early, or drop back and race out of their comfort zone. The most likely prominent slots behind Warrant Holder will be contested by Respond, Yabher, Danger Bay and Will Scarlet, who have the clearest credentials to track the pace at a genuine distance. This race shape — a single front-runner at a honest but uncontested tempo on fast ground — decisively favours horses who can race prominently with cover or mid-to-prominent, travel sweetly into the straight, and quicken from a position of strength; true hold-up closers will find 1m2½f at York on fast ground offers too little room to make up ground in a large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Warrant Holder Controls, Prominent Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Warrant Holder leads uncontested at a fair but unfrenetic tempo and the race is run to suit prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Warrant Holder sets a sustainable gallop, the race shapes into a smooth procession until the straight where those travelling just off the pace have first run; Respond, Yabher and Danger Bay are ideally placed to pounce at the two-furlong pole on fast ground that suits their form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Rises Mid-Race, Staminа Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group — with Auld Toon Loon, Iron Fist or Raammee pushing forward — forces a stronger middle sectional that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: Several natural front-runners compete for position and lift the tempo beyond Warrant Holder's intended pace, turning the race into a true test of stamina over the final three furlongs; horses with proven staying power over 10-12f on fast ground, particularly Dain Ma Nut In and Hand Of God, thrive as rivals tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough for long enough that hold-up horses get an unobstructed run through a tiring field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Castle Stuart, Per Contra and Salam Dubawi, all genuine hold-up types, are able to find a clear passage as the prominent runners empty out; this requires sufficient pace in the early and middle stages, and York's straight gives closers a genuine chance if gaps open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Big Field Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the sheer volume of prominent types causes early crowding, position-switching and a ragged gallop that produces an unpredictable outcome.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners and so many horses seeking the same ground, incidents of interference, checks or riders having to switch lanes are elevated; lower-weighted, lightly-raced or freshened runners who find clear runs — Sportingsilvermine, Altareq or Pearl River — could emerge from the pack unexpectedly.

watchPoints.text: Warrant Holder leads but has multiple natural prominent types — Auld Toon Loon, Raammee and Iron Fist — likely to push forward and challenge for position in the first two furlongs, risking a faster-than-expected early tempo that could compromise all their chances.

Respond is fitted with a hood (hg:h) for the first time or as a continuing aid — watch whether it settles cleanly in a 22-runner field, as any early keenness could cost it the prominent position it needs.

Dain Ma Nut In returns after 142 days off; if the layoff has left it short of peak fitness the chance evaporates, but a fresh horse with a winning profile on this ground is worth monitoring in the market.

The redistribution of so many prominent types — Iron Fist, Raammee, Have Secret, Fantasy Believer among others — means that several horses will race further back than their form suggests is ideal; watch the draw and early positioning for clues as to which manage to secure their natural berth.

Castle Sultan and Salam Dubawi are two of very few true hold-up types in the field — if the pace is genuinely strong across the first mile, both are worth tracking through the final two furlongs as the prominent brigade may empty simultaneously.

races.name: John Smith's Stayers' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and likely sole pace-setter; Ivan Furtado's six-year-old has recent Good-ground form over similar trips but the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild flag — running fully on the lead rather than just prominent may stretch its tactical comfort slightly, though it may benefit most from dictating here.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's four-year-old arrives on a 20-day break with a strong trainer who hits form at 3/14 over the last fortnight; ran well over 2m2f on Good last time and the step to this trip looks a natural progression for a genuinely prominent runner.

runners_data.name: Cruden
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride for an in-form Dan Horsford stable (2/4 in 14 days); the hood suggests a horse who can be keen, and multiple placed efforts over 14-16f on Good and Soft ground highlight solid each-way consistency at this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie, operating at his usual volume (6/53 in 14 days), sends this six-year-old who showed form at 1m6f and 2m on Good ground; ran third over 2m on Good recently, so the trip is within scope, though recent form figures are modest and the wide draw may cost early ground.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old is a genuine front-running type by nature — two wins over 2m on Good ground recently underline stamina and class — but the field's density means it cannot be certain of getting its preferred position and may be forced wider than ideal in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason's eight-year-old is lightly raced in recent weeks (ran just 7 days ago) and holds a win over 1m3f on Good; the hold-up style suits a controlled-pace stayers' contest and placed efforts over staying trips suggest the extra distance is no concern.

runners_data.name: Terrorise
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old has a habit of finishing in rear over Good ground (multiple 6th-13th finishes at similar trips) and recent form figures of 60-006 make it very hard to see a route back into contention even in a slowly-run race; the tailed-off flag is a concern.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Patrick Neville sends this six-year-old back after 169 days off (last ran 34 days ago for this jockey combination) — a high-class staying profile with four wins over 16-20f on Good ground and an unbeaten record on this surface type; naturally wants to race prominently but field congestion will push it toward midfield.

runners_data.name: Division Day
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman claiming 3lb for a horse from Brian Ellison's yard; the four-year-old showed a win and a close second recently, and although the Soft-ground form slightly qualifies enthusiasm for Good to Firm, the staying profile over 1m4f-2m½f looks genuinely suited to this trip.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse but has been reassigned to a midfield role given congestion at the rear; an 0W0P record on similar ground and consistent mid-to-back finishes make improvement hard to project, even on a career-best effort.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old is a true hold-up type by style but has been mapped centrally given the cluster of closers in this field; a win at 1m7f on Soft and a recent form figure of 0 on Good ground over 2m suggest the surface is a mild query and she is likely to need the pace to collapse sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Rock N Roll Pinkie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m½f handicap and should be allowed to bowl along largely unchallenged on Good to Firm ground at York, setting a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a scorching pace. Secret Force, Cruden, and Trojan Sun will press for early prominent positions behind the leader, meaning the front half of the race will be reasonably well-populated without being truly contested at the head of affairs. This field holds more prominent-running types than can all secure their natural berth — Treasure Islands and Cosmic Soul are genuine pace-pressing horses by inclination but are likely to find themselves slotting in behind the true front group rather than sitting where they would ideally want. A single front-runner controlling a genuine staying trip on fast ground at an honest-but-not-suicidal clip will play directly into the hands of those who can travel prominently and conserve enough energy to sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile — hold-up horses face a stiff task if the gallop never fully collapses the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race develops into a sustained stamina test from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Rock N Roll Pinkie controls fractions, the field strings out, and those who have tracked efficiently close up enter the final two furlongs with resources intact; the race becomes a pure test of who stays 2m½f most thoroughly on quick ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough that the front group ties up in the final furlong and a well-positioned hold-up horse arrives with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Valley Of Flowers and Division Day, both genuine hold-up types with strong recent form, get into a rhythm behind a conveniently strung-out field and pick off a tiring front group; the Good to Firm surface rewards their economical travelling style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Cluster Dominated
scenarios.trigger: If two or three of the prominent types push for position early and the pace quickens materially, draining stamina from those committed to racing forward.
scenarios.body: With Cruden, Secret Force, and Trojan Sun all competing for prominent ground, any increase in early tempo raises the chance one sits ideally just off a burning pace and wins doing less work; the scenario suits the horse who finds cover best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie is covered up earlier than expected, the pace collapses, and a late finisher threads through a bunched final furlong.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling gallop over 2m½f bunches the field at the two-furlong pole; a horse producing a sharp finishing burst in a small, tightly-grouped field can spring a surprise regardless of overall stamina.

watchPoints.text: Rock N Roll Pinkie holds the race by the scruff of the neck — if it is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at its own pace, any rival not within striking range by the home turn faces a stern task chasing it down on Good to Firm ground.

Treasure Islands and Cosmic Soul both want to be prominent and may interfere with each other's running in the early stages — watch for traffic issues between the two-furlong marker and the first bend as this cluster jostle for position.

Division Day (36 days off, 3lb claimer Warren Fentiman) is interesting on staying form but the combination of a first run in over a month on quick ground and a claiming rider over 2m½f introduces execution risk — watch whether it settles cleanly in the early stages.

Valley Of Flowers ran just 7 days ago and Joanna Mason will need to judge the pace perfectly in a moderately-run stayers' handicap; if the gallop compresses the field in the straight, the hold-up position could be an advantage, but a slow pace and a bunched finish would suit others more.

Cosmic Soul's 169-day absence (returned 34 days ago) is worth monitoring in the final furlong — its recent win at 1m7f suggests fitness is satisfactory, but a long-distance outing after a break can expose residual ring-rustiness when the race truly tests stamina in the closing stages.

races.name: John Smith's Silver Cup Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Arabian Force
runners_data.note: William Haggas's consistent performer has posted three placed efforts in five recent runs but has not raced in 56 days — the layoff is the key query, and being bumped out of his natural position into a midfield role by the congestion of prominent types tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Oxford
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride on Michael Bell's six-year-old, a dual course-and-distance winner at York on Tapeta; his similar-going turf record is a concern at only 0 wins from 3 starts on genuinely good ground, making the surface switch the central query for his chance.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old is mapped to the rear largely because the prominent positions are oversubscribed — his true style is forward-going, so treat any hold-up win with that caveat; 14 of his last 15 runs have come on similar going, giving him strong ground suitability even if the race shape does not ideally suit him.

runners_data.name: Mount Atlas
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old carries a series of placed efforts on good-to-soft and soft, and while his going record on genuinely good ground is adequate, his natural prominent style will be squeezed for room in this pace-heavy field, pushing him into a midfield role he may not relish.

runners_data.name: Tabletalk
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's consistent stayer has finished second or third in eight of his last fourteen starts on similar going, and he is the highest-OR prominent type most likely to secure the position immediately behind Peace Belle given his reliable jumping-off pace.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Won this race over the same 1m6f York trip on good ground and returns just 13 days later in fine form — her one confirmed front-running role makes her structurally dominant here, though the style-fit tag reminds that her going form outside of good is limited to only four runs.

races.paceDynamic: Peace Belle is the confirmed sole front-runner here, having won over this exact 1m6f York trip on good ground last summer, and with only five rivals she will control tempo from the outset without any direct challenger for the lead. The four genuine prominent types — Arabian Force, Duke Of Oxford, Mount Atlas, and Tabletalk — will jostle for the limited positions just off the pace, while Epic Poet, the least pace-committed of that group, is likely to find herself shuffled furthest back. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can comfortably secure their natural positions; of those, Tabletalk and Mount Atlas, as the highest-rated challengers with the most relevant recent form, are best placed to actually get the berths immediately behind Peace Belle. A solo leader controlling a comfortable, even tempo over 1m6f on good ground at York historically favours those who travel prominently and can mount a sustained challenge from two furlongs out — pure hold-up closers are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Peace Belle Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Peace Belle settles into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout without being headed.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle sets a measured gallop on the front end, and with no rival willing or able to press her, she regulates the race precisely to her own strengths; the sustained nature of 1m6f on fast ground suits a confirmed leader who has already won this contest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Tabletalk and Mount Atlas both track Peace Belle closely and apply pressure from three furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace test of 1m6f brings the highest-rated closers into play as Peace Belle's advantage erodes in the final quarter-mile; Tabletalk's consistent placed form at this trip and similar going makes her the chief beneficiary if the leader's advantage is negated.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If Peace Belle goes too fast early and the field fragments, leaving Epic Poet or Arabian Force to finish fastest.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically quick early pace drains the prominent runners, and a horse that has been able to coast in midfield conserves enough energy to pick up the pieces late; Epic Poet's solid recent form at this trip gives her the best chance among the rear-positioned runners in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a crawl early, turning into a sprint finish that rewards the horse with the sharpest late kick.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling tempo would compress the field and make this a test of finishing speed over the final two furlongs rather than stamina; Duke Of Oxford, who has won twice at this course and distance on a similar surface, would be an unlikely but live threat if he can get a clear run from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Tabletalk or Mount Atlas break sharply enough to secure a position directly behind Peace Belle — if they get squeezed out in the early stages, Peace Belle's lead could become insurmountable.

Monitor Arabian Force's behaviour in the pre-race and opening furlongs after a 56-day absence — any signs of freshness or reluctance to settle in the midfield pack would significantly harm his chance.

Duke Of Oxford has two wins at this course and distance but both came on Tapeta (Fibresand-type surface); his turf form on good ground is poor and punters should treat his course form figures with caution.

Epic Poet's redistribution to hold-up is a structural mapping decision, not a reflection of his true racing style — if he is able to travel prominently early, his solid recent turf form means he becomes a more serious contender than his shown position implies.

races.name: John Smith's Sprint Handicap

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for David O'Meara with Tudhope aboard; two places in five York six-furlong runs on similar going and consistent form, making her one of the most straightforward late-finishing profiles in this race.

runners_data.name: Betties Bay
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner whose entire race depends on controlling the tempo unchallenged; Mason Paetel takes her forward from the gate and four wins in five make her a live force if pace is sustainable, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals her chance is compromised if others press hard.

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's five-year-old is simply outstanding at York on this ground — four wins from five career runs over six furlongs here on Good going is an exceptional course-and-conditions profile that demands respect from any prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Juan Les Pins
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with Michael Appleby who has placed at the highest level of handicap sprinting; prominent style suits this shape but a recent ninth at York on the same trip is a concern worth noting at this age.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Paul Midgley whose recent form figures of 8-6-6-6 on Good and Standard going paint a bleak picture; David Nolan cannot change the pattern if the horse has gone over the top.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's prominent runner who has solid course form but recent figures show he may be finding it tough at this mark; Warren Fentiman's claim is useful but the 9 and 3 in recent form is mixed.

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Julie Camacho whose 44-day absence is the most notable flag; has placed four times in five runs on Good or Good to Firm but the long break and a 5lb claimer on board introduces uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Ruby Red Gove
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old has won twice over six furlongs and placed three times in the last five; a prominent runner who handles Good going and this trip well, and Jonny Peate rides with confidence on form.

runners_data.name: Alpha Magic
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse for the Easterbys who has been placed out to midfield on the map due to runner volume; recent form figures include a wide-margin last place at York on Good going which is hard to look past, and the STYLE_FIT tag further tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's six-year-old carries visor and has been stepping down in trip; the 14-day turnaround is brisk and York six furlongs on Good to Firm represents a sharper test than his last two runs over seven and eight furlongs, but course form over the trip in Good is solid.

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up type wearing tongue-tie and visor who has been consistent at York on Good ground historically; recent form figures are poor (8-10-5-13-8) and he has been beaten comfortably in large-field York sprints this term.

runners_data.name: Bright
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's hold-up runner whose two efforts on York's Good ground produced finishes of 7th and 12th; 36-day break and poor recent form on similar ground make him hard to fancy in a highly competitive 20-runner field.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by style but has spent his recent career racing over five furlongs; bumped to midfield on the map due to field volume, stepping back up to six is an open question and Jason Hart inherits limited claims.

runners_data.name: Rock Opera
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's six-year-old has exceptional course form — two wins and six places in 11 starts on Good going over six furlongs — and Oisin Orr is a high-quality booking; sits prominently and is one of the most reliable pointers to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's seven-year-old has an extraordinary record in similar-going six-furlong handicaps with seven places from nine recent runs; James Sullivan partners a horse who races prominently and hits the board with unusual consistency.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prominent runner with headgear (pads) and a busy campaign; recent six-furlong York form shows he handles the ground and trip but has failed to win in 15 attempts on Good going, suggesting place rather than win potential.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's eight-year-old veteran is a genuine front-running type by nature but has been pushed to midfield on the map because the field is simply too pace-heavy for him to secure his spot; visor-wearing and well-tried in big-field York sprints, his redistribution materially reduces his win prospects.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' two-year-old (recorded as age 2 in data, likely a data anomaly) returning from 259 days off — the longest absence in the race by a significant margin; hold-up style by nature but shuffled to midfield on the map, and the layoff combined with redistribution makes her a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's nine-year-old is a natural front-running/prominent type forced to race from midfield by field dynamics; recent form includes a win and two places in five runs on Good going, but the positional compromise flagged by the redistribution note will blunt his chance if he cannot get daylight early.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old has a win and multiple places over six and seven furlongs and handles Good to Firm well, but his natural prominent racing style has been displaced by the volume of pace horses in this race; racing from further back than he'd prefer, the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful.

races.paceDynamic: Betties Bay is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 20-runner field, she is likely to slot comfortably into a position that suits her, setting a sustainable rather than scorching tempo on Good to Firm ground at York. Glory Hyde, Juan Les Pins, Rock Opera, Fiscal Policy, Havana Rum and Mister Sox are all natural prominent types who will press forward and create a competitive early gallop behind her, though the sheer volume of pace-seekers means several will be forced wider or slightly further back than ideal. The field holds considerably more prominent and front-running horses than can all hold their natural positions — Kats Bob, Good Earth and Magic Boy are true prominent types who will be shuffled back into midfield against their will, and their effectiveness is directly compromised. On this course configuration — a straight six furlongs at York on fast ground with a strong pace set by multiple prominent types — horses with genuine hold-up ability who can track midfield and finish powerfully are best placed, but the sustainable (not suicidal) tempo means the leaders are not guaranteed to blow up; prominent racers who get a clean run on the stands rail or near it retain strong claims.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to stretch the field but Betties Bay and the pressing prominent runners use their forward position to pinch an unassailable break.
scenarios.body: York's straight six favours horses who race handily and get a clean sightline to the line; Glory Hyde's exceptional course form (4 wins from 5 on Good York six furlongs) and Ruby Red Gove's recent winning form make them the standout beneficiaries of a pace-set race where prominent runners grab the best ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to genuinely compromise the prominent brigade, enabling true hold-up types to reel them in across the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Yes I'm Mali and Wreck It Ryley sit further off the pace and have the finishing kick to exploit tired leaders if the gallop is honest; York's long straight gives hold-up horses the best opportunity on any British flat course to close ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Betties Bay Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is not as strong as anticipated and Betties Bay is allowed to dictate at a comfortable tempo without being seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Mason Paetel takes Betties Bay straight to the front from a wide draw and if the prominent runners are content to let her bowl along unchallenged, her current form (four wins in five) and STYLE_FIT flag for her natural role becomes irrelevant — she is on her terms.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Lottery Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant traffic problems at the two-furlong marker, scrambling the race and benefiting horses who happen to find a gap late.
scenarios.body: In a 20-runner sprint on Good to Firm York, pockets can open unpredictably in the final furlong; redistributed prominent types like Good Earth or Kats Bob, forced to race in midfield, could accidentally find themselves in the ideal ground-saving position if the race fragments.

watchPoints.text: Glory Hyde's York course form (4 wins from 5 on Good six furlongs) is exceptional — watch whether Joanna Mason can secure a position just behind Betties Bay on the rail, as any interference or wide draw could compromise her chance in a 20-runner sprint.

The sheer number of prominent types — Glory Hyde, Juan Les Pins, Rock Opera, Fiscal Policy, Havana Rum, Mister Sox and Ruby Red Gove — all pressing forward behind Betties Bay risks a fierce early pace that could compress finishing positions and produce a blanket finish in the final furlong.

Kats Bob, Good Earth and Magic Boy are all genuine prominent types forced to race in midfield against their natural instincts; watch whether any of them get outpaced early or become racing passengers, as their redistribution significantly undermines their ability to produce their best form.

Educating Rita returns from 259 days off — by far the longest layoff in the field — and faces a hot 20-runner sprint handicap first time back; watch the market for any significant support, as stable confidence will be the only meaningful guide.

Betties Bay's draw and early position are critical — if she is forced wide or another horse disputes the lead, the sustainable pace scenario collapses and hold-up types like Yes I'm Mali and Wreck It Ryley become considerably more dangerous.
